# UC Schools: Attractive for So Many Reasons
The University of California (UC) system is a paragon of public higher education in the United States. It's diverse campuses consistently rank among the very best public universities in the US.

...

Established in 1868 with its flagship campus in Berkeley, the UC system has grown exponentially, but still barely keeps pace with demand, and now boasts nine unique campuses in locations across California.

...

And, let’s not forget California’s emerging biotech hubs, Hollywood’s global footprint in entertainment culture and business, as well as the state’s robust agricultural sector and highly diverse workforce…

There are 9 undergraduate campuses in the University of California system. These include UC Berkeley, UC Davis, UC Irvine, UCLA, UC Merced, UC Riverside, UC San Diego, UC Santa Barbara, and UC Santa Cruz.
As for your second question, each University of California campus requires its own application. Although there's only one application form through the UC system's online platform, you will select each campus you wish to apply to individually through this application.
You'll pay an application fee for each campus, as well. The same application will be sent to each of the campuses you select, so make sure your application is broad enough to cover all the UC schools you are interested in.
